claims.text: As-cast bulk HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast bulk HfMoTaTiZr has a fully dense microstructure.
HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperatures around 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention is to fabricate HfMoTaTiZr as a topology-optimized additive-manufactured cellular lattice.
Introducing a designed void fraction through a lattice architecture will reduce the component's effective overall density.
Additive manufacturing can produce fully dense HfMoTaTiZr struts that retain microstructural characteristics similar to the as-cast alloy.
A post-build heat treatment can refine or restore the strut microstructure without changing alloy composition.
Fully dense lattice struts will preserve the intrinsic room-temperature mechanical strength of HfMoTaTiZr.
Fully dense lattice struts will preserve the intrinsic high-temperature load-bearing capability of HfMoTaTiZr around 1000 °C.
The lattice will transfer load effectively through its dense struts at both ambient and elevated temperatures.
Topology-optimized lattice HfMoTaTiZr will have significantly lower overall density than monolithic as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Topology-optimized lattice HfMoTaTiZr will retain comparable area-normalized compressive strength at room temperature.
Topology-optimized lattice HfMoTaTiZr will retain comparable area-normalized compressive strength at approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed applicability boundary is compressive loading from ambient temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
Performance under dynamic or fatigue loading is not predicted.
